title: Healthleap raises $38M for its AI that flags hospital patients who may need a closer look
key_facts: Healthleap has raised $38 million in seed and Series A funding; TechCrunch says it learned this exclusively.
The financing includes an $8 million seed round co-led by Sequoia Capital and First Round Capital, and a $30 million Series A led by Hummingbird Ventures; valuation not disclosed.
Founded in South Africa in 2022 by siblings Jemima and Josiah Meyer; Josiah Meyer is CEO and co-founder.
The platform reads patient records using language models to find notes that suggest malnutrition or delirium, and is deployed in more than 50 hospitals.
Customers named include Penn Medicine, Cedars-Sinai, Intermountain, Houston Methodist and Emory Healthcare.
The company says it does not diagnose patients, only highlights items for review; the company says every customer has seen a 5x hard ROI or more.
At the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania the company claims $23.8 million in annualised financial impact.
quote_evidence: The company notes that its software doesn’t diagnose patients, only highlights items for additional review.
We use the hard ROI that the hospital finance team validates and attributes to us as the measurable ROI.
why_it_matters_hint: Hospital software that flags at-risk patients could help patients who are missed, but the return figures are company claims.
notes: Full text from TechCrunch read; page includes unrelated sidebar text which was ignored. ROI and impact figures are the company's claims as quoted by its CEO.
